entities.summary: San Roberto Bellarmino is a church in Rome founded by Pope Pius XI in 1933. It followed the canonisation of the Jesuit Cardinal Robert Bellarmine (1542–1621) in 1930, and his being named a Doctor of the Church in 1931. The architect Clemente Busiri Vici made the designs in the years 1931–1933. Construction took more than two decades, and it was consecrated in 1959 by Archbishop Luigi Traglia. It is served by the Jesuits, and has a mosaic by Renato Tomassi and a high altar donated by Beniamino Gigli. San Roberto Bellarmino church is a church building in Europe, established in 1931. historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: San Roberto Bellarmino church's consecration in 1959 marked a significant milestone for the Jesuit order, solidifying its presence in Rome. The church's design and architecture reflect Clemente Busiri Vici's innovative style.
